LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 10.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY: INTERACTIVE LISTENING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.1: Listening and Speaking 10.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Interactive Listening
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 10.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Interactive Listening, part of Strand 10 in Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we take turns in a conversation? 2. What are some of the moods/feelings we can show during a conversation?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. pick out the sound /h/ as in holiday, /j/ as in yam and /eə/ as in air, from an audio text,

2. listen to a text on proper use of leisure time and say words and phrases with the sound /h/,

3. take turns during short interviews, debates and discussions on grade appropriate topics,

4. interrupt appropriately during a class discussion, interview or debate,

5. perform a choral verse (about six stanzas) or conversational 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. pick out the sound /h/ as in holiday, /j/ as in yam and /eə/ as in air, from an audio text,
2. listen to a text on proper use of leisure time and say words and phrases with the sound /h/,
3. take turns during short interviews, debates and discussions on grade appropriate topics,
4. interrupt appropriately during a class discussion, interview or debate,
5. perform a choral verse (about six stanzas) or conversational 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 10.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Interactive Listening together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Collaboration: The learner’s ability to contribute to group decision making is enhanced by reciting choral poems

with peers.

• Self-efficacy: The learner’s ability to confidently share what they have learnt is developed as they take turns and

interrupt effectively in conversations.

Values:
Responsibility: This is inculcated in the learner as they engage in assigned tasks and pick out the sound /h/, /j/ and

/eə/ from an audio text.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills: The learner is able to communicate effectively through acquisition of interactive listening skills.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the skills of interactive listening to group interactions in the learning of Creative Arts.
